content:
Ashley Nguyen: Heads up — seeing a spike of SSO login failures after last night's KMS rotation. Appears to block JIT provisioning and role assignment for some users in EU region.
Samir Patel: Can you paste the error lines from the provisioner logs?
Ashley Nguyen: sure, here's the main snippet we see:
```
okta-provisioner[1234]: ERROR: KMS_DECRYPT_FAILED: failed to decrypt assertion-key for user=alice@example.com, cause=AccessDenied
okta-provisioner[1234]: context: key_alias=alias/redwood/okta-assertion-key, key_id=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111111111:key/abcd-rotated
okta-provisioner[1234]: result: fallback=minimal_identity, roles_assigned=[]
```
Jess Ortiz: Is that our KMS rotation or an Okta change? cc @Kevin Cho
Ashley Nguyen: Rotation happened last night via rotation-batch-2026-03-19. Alias was updated to new key version, but looks like the service principal lost Decrypt permission on the new key.
Carla Ruiz: Wait — we encrypt SAML attributes using KMS and then decrypt inside the provisioner? If decrypt fails do we block provisioning?
Samir Patel: Correct. Flow: Okta -> SAML assertion -> our edge encrypts sensitive attributes with KMS alias -> provisioner calls KMS:Decrypt -> parse attributes -> map roles. If Decrypt fails, current fallback is to continue with minimal identity (email only) which causes role mapping to be skipped -> user ends up with no roles/guest.
Ashley Nguyen: Example from logs: `JIT provision failed: missing roles; assertion_decrypt_error=true; fallback=limited` — customers report account creation failed or users lost admin roles.
security-bot: ALERT: Incident detected - 10m window - 120 failed JIT provisions (threshold=30). Pager triggered.
Samir Patel: Impact summary?
Ashley Nguyen: Affected: EU dedicated tenants using Okta SAML with JIT. Some newly onboarded users couldn't get admin roles; some login attempts failed outright. CS ticket volume increasing.
Samir Patel: Immediate remediation plan: re-grant kms:Decrypt to service-account:okta-provisioner-prod for the new key version, or roll alias back to previous key id. Who can update KMS/IAM? @Kevin Cho
Kevin Cho: On it. I'll validate perms and either update key policy or repoint the alias. Re-granting decrypt permission now.
Jess Ortiz: We should also treat this as a postmortem candidate. We need better runbooks for key rotation and a canary phase. Also add clearer error surface so customers see useful messages.
Carla Ruiz: Also consider changing fallback behavior. Right now we silently downgrade roles; that's dangerous. Two options: 1) fail hard (deny) so customers see a 5xx immediately, or 2) keep fail-open but add louder analytics/alerts. My vote: fail-closed until we have proven canary.
Samir Patel: I agree fail-closed for role-sensitive attrs. But we need a smoother customer communication plan.
Ashley Nguyen: For immediate mitigation I temporarily repointed alias `alias/redwood/okta-assertion-key` back to previous key-id and re-ran a few provisioning flows. Success rate climbed back up.
Kevin Cho: Verified: after alias revert, decrypt success rate ~99.8% and JIT provisioning resumed. Pushing IAM patch to ensure service principal has decrypt on future keys.
security-bot: AUDIT: KMS alias change detected by user Kevin Cho at ts=2487654350. AuditID=AZ-9f8a.
Jess Ortiz: Follow-ups: 1) add canary rotation runbook + checklist, 2) require rotation CI job to update IAM/key policy for provisioner principals, 3) instrument `assertion_decrypt_error` metric and lower alert threshold, 4) update fallback behavior for role mapping with explicit opt-in.
Carla Ruiz: Owners: Kevin -> perms fix + PR for key policy. Ashley -> monitoring + customer outreach. Samir -> code changes to error handling and tests. Jess -> postmortem doc + runbook.
Kevin Cho: Opening infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/483 (grant decrypt to okta-provisioner-prod on rotation)
Samir Patel: Also need a reconciliation script to scan users created in the last 24h and re-apply role mappings for any that were downgraded because of this. I'll pick this up after the code changes.
Ashley Nguyen: Noted. I'll ping CS and send an incident update to affected tenant contacts.
Jess Ortiz: Good triage. Add timeline and root cause to postmortem when we have it.
Ashley Nguyen: Thanks everyone. Will update this thread as we close items. :thumbsup:
